4. Rabbi Ephraim Fischel, died in תי״ג (1653) *י

As we see, approximately 27 years elapsed between the deaths of the two rabbis mentioned above. This means that in the interim there was certainly another rabbi, and perhaps more than one rabbi.

Once again, we are dealing with lineage. Rabbi Ephraim Fischel was the father-in-law of the famous Kraków rabbi, Rabbi Leib Fischel. He was called Rabbi Leib der Hoicher. He was regarded as a holy man. His father, too, was greatly revered. He was called Rabbi Zechariah the Prophet, and he was a great-grandson of the famous Rabbi Saul Wahl, the legendary king of Poland.

This family was one of the famous families in Poland. The progenitor, Rabbi Fischel, was the first chief rabbi (head rabbi) of Poland, in the time of Sigismund I. He later died as a martyr for the sanctification of God’s name.”<

From this Rabbi Leib branched a large family, and his great-grandchildren were born in Mezhyrich. Two of them were Rabbi Abishl Frankfurter and Rabbi Mordecai Liser.

Rabbi Solomon Zalman, died in ת״כ (1660)

He was almost certainly rabbi in Luków after the aforementioned Rabbi Ephraim Fischel.

The rabbis of Luków, as one can see, were steeped in illustrious lineage. Rabbi—
